text:
kai: Quick one— customers hitting weird import failures when our JS/TS SDK is consumed from pnpm workspaces and built for edge (Next.js/Edge Functions, Cloudflare, Fastly). Error: `Could not resolve '@redwood/sdk' -> attempted '/workspace/node_modules/.pnpm/..../@redwood+sdk@1.2.3'` only in CI/deploy. Local npm install works. Anyone seen this exact pnpm virtual store + exports / typing combo?

zoe: Yup. Root cause is usually bundler resolver + conditional `exports` + pnpm's virtual store symlink layout. Many edge bundlers (and some versions of esbuild/rollup plugins) expect a simple file at package root. If exports point to nested paths, resolver may follow realpath into pnpm store and that path doesn't get packaged into the deploy artifact.

matt: Which bundler + Node target? Also are consumers importing subpaths like `@redwood/sdk/orm`? Those deep imports often break with exports maps.

kai: Using Vite for local dev, but the failing CI step is Next.js edge build (esbuild under the hood) and Cloudflare Pages publishing. Consumers do sometimes import `@redwood/sdk/metrics` (we provide a few named subpaths). SDK package.json has: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs.js" }, "./metrics": "./dist/esm/metrics.mjs" }, "types": "dist/index.d.ts".

linh: A few concrete mitigations we use internally: 1) publish a small root ESM shim at `index.mjs` that just `export * from './dist/esm/index.mjs'` and set `".": {"import":"./index.mjs","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs.js"}` in exports. 2) include `"./package.json":"./package.json"` in exports so bundlers don't try to read package.json across symlink boundaries. 3) make sure `.d.ts` files are packaged next to dist and keep a top-level `types` field.

zoe: Also consider adding `"./*": "./dist/*"` style fallback exports if you must support subpath imports, but beware of npm's export semantics. Alternatively, avoid advertising subpath imports and provide named exports from the root index to keep resolution trivial for edge packagers.

matt: For typings, some TS consumers (and editors) don't look inside `exports` for `types`. Keep `types` at top-level and add `typesVersions` if you need legacy support. And ensure the published tarball actually contains the d.ts: pnpm pack can behave differently with workspace: protocol.

kai: We tried three approaches: (A) tell customers to set `nodeLinker=node-modules` in CI (works but heavy-handed), (B) change SDK exports to root shim (much better UX), (C) in sample-app CI do `pnpm pack` + `npm i ./sdk-*.tgz` to emulate published layout during build. Root shim + packaged d.ts fixed most of our cases.

linh: Add a CI repro: 1) create pnpm workspace with sdk and app; 2) `pnpm i` (default nodeLinker), 3) in app -> `node node_modules/.bin/esbuild src/edge.ts --bundle` or run `next build` for edge target. If esbuild resolves to a pnpm store path, fail the test. For automated tests, `pnpm pack` the SDK and `npm i` the tgz in a clean temp dir then run the bundle step to assert no store paths are referenced.

zoe: Edge case we hit: Yarn PnP + Node 18 Runtimes—some packagers assume `require` can read package.json on disk. If you publish with exports but the runtime expects package.json accessible, include the package.json export mapping to avoid runtime errors.

matt: Implementation note for SDK maintainers: keep exports minimal, prefer ESM-first root entry, and avoid exposing internal file paths. Also add a tiny integration test that builds a minimal edge app against the packaged SDK (tgz) as part of release pipeline.

kai: I'll open a PR with: index.mjs shim, exports simplified to root mapping + package.json export, top-level types field, and a sample-app CI job that packs the SDK and runs an edge bundle step. I'll also add a short DevEx FAQ entry.

devex-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-391: "SDK: prevent pnpm virtual-store resolution leakage for edge builds — add root ESM shim, export package.json, include d.ts, add sample-app CI repro" :white_check_mark:

zoe: Thanks! This should reduce a bunch of on-call deploy tickets for sample-app users.
